children.text: vande mukundamaravindadalāyatākṣaṃ kundenduśaṅkhadaśanaṃ śiśugopaveṣam /
children.translated_text: I bow to <s>Mukunda</s>, whose eyes are long like lotus petals, whose teeth are [bright] like jasmine buds, the moon, and conch-shells, who wears the garb of a young cowherd boy,

children.text: indrādidevagaṇavanditapādapīṭhaṃ vṛndāvanālayamahaṃ vasudevasūnum || 1 ||
children.translated_text: whose footstool is worshipped by the hosts of gods led by <s>Indra</s> — I [bow to] Him, the son of <s>Vasudeva</s>, whose abode is <s>Vṛndāvana</s>. (1)

children.text: jayatu jayatu devo devakīnandano 'yaṃ jayatu jayatu kṛṣṇo vṛṣṇivaṃśapradīpaḥ /
children.translated_text: Victory, victory to the god who is the joy of <s>Devakī</s>! Victory, victory to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the lamp of the <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> dynasty!

children.text: jayatu jayatu meghaśyāmalaḥ komalāṅgo jayatu jayatu pṛthvībhāranāśo mukundaḥ || 2 ||
children.translated_text: Victory, victory to Him who is dark as a cloud and tender of limb! Victory, victory to <s>Mukunda</s>, the destroyer of the earth's burden! (2)

children.text: mukunda mūrdhnā praṇipatya yāce bhavantamekāntamiyantamartham /
children.translated_text: O <s>Mukunda</s>! Bowing my head, I ask of you this one single thing:

children.text: avismṛtistvaccaraṇāravinde bhave bhave me 'sti bhavatprasādāt || 3 ||
children.translated_text: May there be unfailing remembrance of your lotus feet, in birth after birth, by your grace. (3)

children.text: śrīmukundapadāmbhojamadhunaḥ paramādbhutam /
children.translated_text: The supreme, wondrous honey of the lotus feet of <s>Śrī Mukunda</s> —

children.text: yatpāyino na muhyanti muhyanti yadapāyinaḥ || 4 ||
children.translated_text: those who drink it are not deluded; those who do not drink it are deluded. (4)

children.text: nāhaṃ vande tava caraṇayordvandvamadvandvahetoḥ kumbhīpākaṃ gurumapi hare nārakaṃ nāpanetum /
children.translated_text: I do not worship the pair of your feet, O <s>Hari</s>, to rid myself of the opposites [of pleasure and pain], nor to escape the terrible <s>Kumbhīpāka</s> hell,

children.text: ramyā rāmā mṛdutanulatā nandane nāpi rantuṃ bhāve bhāve hṛdayabhavane bhāvaye 'haṃ bhavantam || 5 ||
children.translated_text: nor to sport with lovely women of tender vine-like bodies in <s>Nandana</s> [garden] — but in birth after birth, in the temple of my heart, I contemplate you. (5)

children.text: nāsthā dharme na vasunicaye naiva kāmopabhoge yadbhāvyaṃ tadbhavatu bhagavanpūrvakarmānurūpam /
children.translated_text: I have no attachment to duty (<s>dharma</s>), nor to the accumulation of wealth, nor to the enjoyment of desires; whatever is destined to be, let it be, O Lord, in accordance with past <s>karma</s>.

children.text: etatprārthyaṃ mama bahumataṃ janmajanmāntare 'pi tvatpādāmbhoruhayugagatā niścalā bhaktirastu || 6 ||
children.translated_text: This alone is my prayer, greatly cherished: may there be, in birth after birth, unwavering devotion (<s>bhakti</s>) fixed upon the pair of your lotus feet. (6)

children.text: divi vā bhuvi vā mamāstu vāso narake vā narakāntake prakāmam /
children.translated_text: Whether my dwelling be in heaven or on earth, or indeed in hell — [let it be] wherever, at the will of the destroyer of hell;

children.text: avadhīritaśāradāravindau caraṇau te maraṇe 'pi cintayāmi || 7 ||
children.translated_text: your feet, which put to shame the autumn lotuses, I contemplate even at the moment of death. (7)

children.text: sarasijanayane saśaṅkhacakre murabhidi mā virameha citta rantum /
children.translated_text: O lotus-eyed one! O bearer of the conch and discus! O slayer of <s>Mura</s>! Do not cease, O mind, to delight here!

children.text: sukhakaramaparaṃ na jātu jāne haricaraṇasmaraṇāmṛtena tulyam || 8 ||
children.translated_text: I know of no other happiness equal to the nectar of remembering the feet of <s>Hari</s>. (8)

children.text: mā bhairmandamano vicintya bahudhā yāmīściraṃ yātanā nāmī naḥ prabhavanti pāparipavaḥ svāmī nanu śrīdharaḥ /
children.translated_text: Fear not, O timid mind, thinking much of the long torments of <s>Yama</s>! Those waves of sin have no power over us, for our master is none other than <s>Śrīdhara</s> [the bearer of <s>Śrī</s>].

children.text: ālasyaṃ vyapanīya bhaktisulabhaṃ dhyāyasva nārāyaṇaṃ lokasya vyasanāpanodanakaro dāsasya kiṃ na kṣamaḥ || 9 ||
children.translated_text: Cast off laziness and meditate on <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, who is easily attained through devotion. Is He who removes the afflictions of the world not capable [of helping] His servant? (9)

children.text: bhavajaladhimagādhaṃ dustaraṃ nistareyaṃ kathamahamiti ceto mā sma gāḥ kātaratvam /
children.translated_text: The ocean of worldly existence (<s>bhava</s>) is fathomless and impossible to cross — 'How shall I cross it?' — O mind, do not give in to cowardice!

children.text: sarasijadṛśi deve tāvakī bhaktirekā narakabhidi niṣaṇṇā tārayiṣyatyavaśyam || 10 ||
children.translated_text: Devotion to you alone, fixed upon the lotus-eyed god, the destroyer of hell, will surely deliver [you] across. (10)

children.text: tṛṣṇātoye madanapavanoddhūtamohormimāle dārāvarte sahajatanayagrāhasaṃghākule ca /
children.translated_text: In the great ocean called <s>saṃsāra</s> — with thirst for its waters, with waves of delusion raised by the wind of desire, with the whirlpool of wife [and family], teeming with crocodile-shoals of innate children —

children.text: saṃsārākhye mahati jaladhau majjatāṃ nastridhāmanpādāmbhoje varada bhavato bhaktināve prasīda || 11 ||
children.translated_text: for those who are drowning, O granter of boons, be gracious! [Let] the boat of devotion (<s>bhakti</s>) to your lotus feet [rescue us], O three-aboded one! (11)

children.text: pṛthvīreṇuraṇuḥ payāṃsi kaṇikāḥ phalguḥ sphuliṅgo laghustejo niḥśvasanaṃ maruttanutaraṃ randhraṃ susūkṣmaṃ nabhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Earth is [but] a speck of dust, waters [but] droplets, fire [but] a tiny spark, wind [but] a faint breath, space [but] a minute hole,

children.text: kṣudrā rudrapitāmahaprabhṛtayaḥ kīṭāḥ samastāḥ surā dṛṣṭe yatra sa tāvako vijayate bhūmāvadhūtāvadhiḥ || 12 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Pitāmaha</s> [Brahmā], and the rest are [mere] insects, and all the gods are insignificant — compared to Him, your glory, whose greatness is beyond limit, who is triumphant when beheld. (12)

children.text: āmnāyābhyasanānyaraṇyaruditaṃ kṛcchravratānyanvahaṃ medaśchedapadāni pūrtavidhayaḥ sarve hutaṃ bhasmani /
children.translated_text: Study of the sacred texts, weeping in the wilderness, daily practice of severe vows, cutting away of fat [through austerity], acts of public merit — all [are like] oblations poured into ashes,

children.text: tīrthānāmavagāhanāni ca gajasnānaṃ vinā yatpadadvandvāmbhoruhasaṃstutiṃ vijayate devaḥ sa nārāyaṇaḥ || 13 ||
children.translated_text: and immersions in holy fords are [mere] elephant-baths — without the praise of the pair of lotus feet of that victorious God, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. (13)

children.text: ānanda govinda mukunda rāma nārāyaṇānanta nirāmayeti /
children.translated_text: <s>Ānanda</s>, <s>Govinda</s>, <s>Mukunda</s>, <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Ananta</s>, <s>Nirāmaya</s> —

children.text: vaktuṃ samartho 'pi na vakti kaścidaho janānāṃ vyasanāni mokṣe || 14 ||
children.translated_text: though one is able to utter [these names], no one utters them. Alas, the delusions of people regarding liberation! (14)

children.text: kṣīrasāgarataraṅgaśīkarāsāratārakitacārumūrtaye /
children.translated_text: To Him whose beautiful form is sprinkled with the spray of the waves of the ocean of milk,

children.text: bhogibhogaśayanīyaśāyine mādhavāya madhuvidviṣe namaḥ || 15 ||
children.translated_text: to Him who reclines upon the bed of the serpent's coils, to <s>Mādhava</s>, the enemy of <s>Madhu</s> — obeisance! (15)

children.text: vātsalyādabhayapradānasamayādārtārtinirvāpaṇādaudāryādaghaśoṣaṇādagaṇitaśreyaḥpadaprāpaṇāt /
children.translated_text: For His tenderness in granting fearlessness, for His soothing of the sufferings of the afflicted, for His generosity, for His burning away of sins, and for leading to the immeasurable station of blessedness —

children.text: sevyaḥ śrīpatireva sarvajagatāmekāntataḥ sākṣiṇaḥ prahlādaśca vibhīṣaṇaśca karirāṭ pāñcālyahalyā dhruvaḥ || 16 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śrīpati</s> (the Lord of <s>Śrī</s>) alone is to be served, [as witnessed by] the exclusive witnesses for all the worlds: <s>Prahlāda</s>, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, the king of elephants [<s>Gajendra</s>], <s>Draupadī</s>, <s>Ahalyā</s>, and <s>Dhruva</s>. (16)

children.text: nāthe śrīpuruṣottame trijagatāmekādhipe cetasā sevye svasya padasya dātari pare nārāyaṇe tiṣṭhati /
children.translated_text: When <s>Śrī Puruṣottama</s> stands [before us], the sole sovereign of the three worlds, to be served with the heart, the bestower of His own supreme abode, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>,

children.text: yaṃ kaṃcitpuruṣādhamaṃ katipayagrāmeśamalpādarthadaṃ sevāyai mṛgayāmahe naramaho mūḍhā varākā vayam || 17 ||
children.translated_text: we seek out for service some wretched, lowly person, the headman of a few villages, who gives a trifle — alas, how foolish and pitiful we are! (17)

children.text: bho lokāḥ śṛṇuta prasūtimaraṇavyādheścikitsāmimāṃ yogajñāḥ samudāharanti munayo yāṃ yājñavalkyādayaḥ /
children.translated_text: O people! Hear this prescription for the disease of birth and death—that which the sages learned in <s>yoga</s>, such as <s>Yājñavalkya</s> and others, proclaim:

children.text: antarjyotirameyamekamamṛtaṃ kṛṣṇākhyamāpīyatāṃ yatpītaṃ paramauṣadhaṃ vitanute nirvāṇamātyantikam || 18 ||
children.translated_text: Let the inner light, immeasurable, singular, immortal, called <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, be drunk; for when drunk, this supreme medicine produces absolute <s>nirvāṇa</s> (liberation). || 18 ||

children.text: baddhenāñjalinā natena śirasā gātraiḥ saromodgamaiḥ kaṇṭhena savaragadgadena nayanenodgīrṇabāṣpāmbunā /
children.translated_text: With cupped hands joined, with head bowed, with limbs bearing hair standing on end, with throat choked and faltering, with eyes overflowing with tears,

children.text: nityaṃ tvaccaraṇāravindayugaladhyānāmṛtāsvādināmasmākaṃ sarasīruhākṣa satataṃ saṃpadyatāṃ jīvitam || 19 ||
children.translated_text: may the life of us who constantly relish the nectar of meditating on the pair of your lotus-feet, O Lotus-eyed One (<s>Sarasīruhākṣa</s>), be ever fulfilled. || 19 ||

children.text: tattvaṃ bruvāṇāni paraṃ parasmādaho kṣarantīva sudhāṃ padāni /
children.translated_text: Uttering the supreme truth beyond the highest—ah, as though dripping nectar, [these] words!

children.text: āvartaya prāñjalirasmi jihve nāmāni nārāyaṇagocarāṇi || 20 ||
children.translated_text: Revolve [them], O tongue—I stand with joined palms—the names that pertain to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. || 20 ||

children.text: idaṃ śarīraṃ pariṇāmapeśalaṃ patatyavaśyaṃ ślathasaṃdhi jarjaram /
children.translated_text: This body, rendered fragile by decay, will inevitably fall, loose-jointed and decrepit;

children.text: kimauṣadhaiḥ kliśyasi mūḍha durmate nirāmayaṃ kṛṣṇarasāyanaṃ piba || 21 ||
children.translated_text: why do you torment yourself with medicines, O foolish, wicked-minded one? Drink the disease-free elixir of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>! || 21 ||

children.text: śrīmannāma procya nārāyaṇākhyaṃ yena prāptā vāñchitaṃ pāpino 'pi /
children.translated_text: By merely pronouncing the auspicious name called <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, even sinners have attained their desires;

children.text: hā naḥ pūrvaṃ vākpravṛttā na tasmiṃstena prāptaṃ garbhavāsādiduḥkham || 22 ||
children.translated_text: alas, our speech was not directed toward that [name] before—because of that, we have obtained the suffering of dwelling in the womb and the rest. || 22 ||

children.text: mā drākṣaṃ kṣīṇapuṇyānkṣaṇamapi bhavato bhaktihīnānpadābje mā śrauṣaṃ śravyabaddhaṃ tava caritamapāsyānyadākhyānajātam /
children.translated_text: May I never see, even for a moment, those of exhausted merit who lack devotion to your lotus-feet; may I never hear any other tale, abandoning the narration of your deeds, worthy of hearing;

children.text: mā sprākṣaṃ mādhava tvāmapi bhuvanapate cetasāpahnuvānaṃ mā bhūvaṃ tvatsaparyāvyatikararahito janmajanmāntare 'pi || 23 ||
children.translated_text: may I never touch, O <s>Mādhava</s>, one who mentally denies you, O Lord of the world; may I never be deprived of the performance of your worship, even in birth after birth. || 23 ||

children.text: madana parihara sthitiṃ madīye manasi mukundapadāravindadhāmni /
children.translated_text: O <s>Madana</s> (god of love), abandon your station in my mind, which is the abode of the lotus-feet of <s>Mukunda</s>;

children.text: haranayanakṛśānunā kṛśo 'si smarasi na cakraparākramaṃ murāreḥ || 24 ||
children.translated_text: you have been emaciated by the fire of <s>Hara</s>'s (Śiva's) eye—do you not remember the prowess of the discus of <s>Murāri</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>)? || 24 ||

children.text: dārā vārākaravarasutā te 'ṅgajo 'yaṃ viriñcaḥ stotā vedastava suragaṇo bhṛtyavargaḥ prasādaḥ /
children.translated_text: Your wife is the best daughter of the ocean (<s>Lakṣmī</s>); your son is <s>Viriñca</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>); your panegyrist is the <s>Veda</s>; the host of gods is your band of servants; your grace is

children.text: muktirmadhye jagadavikalaṃ tāvake devakī te mātā mittraṃ balaripusutastattvato 'nyanna jāne || 25 ||
children.translated_text: liberation; the world entire is within you; <s>Devakī</s> is your mother; your friend is <s>Bala</s> (Balarāma), the son of the enemy's foe—truly, I know nothing else [beyond you]. || 25 ||

children.text: jihve kīrtaya keśavaṃ muraripuṃ ceto bhaja śrīdharaṃ pāṇidvandva samarcayācyutakathāṃ śrotradvaya tvaṃ śruṇu /
children.translated_text: O tongue, praise <s>Keśava</s>, the enemy of <s>Mura</s>! O mind, worship <s>Śrīdhara</s>! O pair of hands, serve [him]! O pair of ears, listen to the story of <s>Acyuta</s>!

children.text: kṛṣṇaṃ lokaya locanadvaya harergacchāṅghriyugmālayaṃ jighra ghrāṇa mukundapādatulasīṃ murdhannamādhokṣajam || 26 ||
children.translated_text: O pair of eyes, behold <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>! O pair of feet, go to the temple of <s>Hari</s>! O nose, smell the <s>tulasī</s> at <s>Mukunda</s>'s feet! O head, bow to <s>Adhokṣaja</s> (the Transcendent One)! || 26 ||

children.text: yatkṛṣṇapraṇipātadhūlidhavalaṃ tadvai śiraḥ syācchubhaṃ te netre tamasojjhite surucire yābhyāṃ harirdṛśyate /
children.translated_text: That head is truly blessed which is whitened by the dust of prostration before <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>; those eyes are beautiful, freed from darkness, through which <s>Hari</s> is seen;

children.text: sā buddhirniyamairyamaiśca vimalā yā mādhavadhyāyinī sā jihvāmṛtavarṣiṇī pratipadaṃ yā stauti nārāyaṇam || 27 ||
children.translated_text: that intellect is pure through disciplines and restraints which meditates on <s>Mādhava</s>; that tongue rains nectar which praises <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> at every step. || 27 ||

children.text: bhaktadveṣibhujaṃgagāruḍamaṇistrailokyarakṣāmaṇirgopīlocanacātakāmbudamaṇiḥ saundaryamudrāmaṇiḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Garuḍa</s>-gem (antidote) against the serpent of hostility toward devotees, the jewel that protects the three worlds, the rain-cloud jewel for the <s>cātaka</s>-bird-eyes of the <s>gopīs</s>, the seal-jewel of beauty,

children.text: śrīkāntāmaṇirukmiṇīghanakucadvandvaikabhūṣāmaṇiḥ śreyo dhyeyaśikhāmṇirdiśatu no gopālacūḍāmaṇiḥ || 28 ||
children.translated_text: the gem of <s>Śrī's</s> (Lakṣmī's) beloved, the sole ornamental jewel for the pair of heavy breasts of <s>Rukmiṇī</s>, the crown-jewel of meditation for the highest good—may the crest-jewel of the cowherds (<s>Gopālacūḍāmaṇi</s>) bestow blessings upon us. || 28 ||

children.text: śatrucchedaikamantraṃ sakalamupaniṣadvākyasaṃpūjyamantraṃ saṃsārottāramantraṃ samuditamanasāṃ saṅganiryāṇamantram /
children.translated_text: The sole <s>mantra</s> for destroying enemies, the <s>mantra</s> worshipped by all the words of the <s>Upaniṣads</s>, the <s>mantra</s> for crossing the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>, the <s>mantra</s> of departure from worldly association for those of uplifted minds,

children.text: sarvaiśvaryaikamantraṃ vyasanabhujagasaṃdaṣṭasaṃtrāṇamantraṃ jihve śrīkṛṣṇamantraṃ japa japa satataṃ janmasāphalyamantram || 29 ||
children.translated_text: the sole <s>mantra</s> of all sovereignty, the <s>mantra</s> of rescue for those bitten by the serpent of calamity—O tongue, recite constantly the <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> <s>mantra</s>, the <s>mantra</s> that makes birth fruitful! || 29 ||

children.text: vyāmohoddalanauṣadhaṃ munimanovṛttipravṛttyauṣadhaṃ daityānarthakarauṣadhaṃ trijagatāṃ saṃjīvanaikauṣadham /
children.translated_text: The medicine that uproots delusion, the medicine that sets the minds of sages in motion, the medicine that brings ruin to demons, the sole life-restoring medicine of the three worlds,

children.text: bhaktārtipraśamauṣadhaṃ bhavabhayapradhvaṃsi divyauṣadhaṃ śreyaḥprāptikarauṣadhaṃ piba manaḥ śrīkṛṣṇanāmauṣadham || 30 ||
children.translated_text: the medicine that soothes the affliction of devotees, the divine medicine that destroys the fear of worldly existence, the medicine that brings the attainment of the highest good—O mind, drink the medicine of the name of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>! || 30 ||

children.text: āścaryametaddhi manuṣyaloke sudhāṃ parityajya viṣaṃ pibanti /
children.translated_text: How astonishing this is in the human world: abandoning nectar, they drink poison!

children.text: nāmāni nārāyaṇagocarāṇi tyaktvānyavācaḥ kuhakāḥ paṭhanti || 31 ||
children.translated_text: Forsaking the names that pertain to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the deluded ones recite other words. || 31 ||

children.text: lāṭīnetrapuṭīpayodharaghaṭīrevātaṭīduṣkuṭīpāṭīradrumavarṇanena kavibhirmūḍhairdinaṃ nīyate /
children.translated_text: By foolish poets, the day is spent in describing the eye-glances of courtesans, the pitchers of their breasts, their waist-regions, and their wicked bowers along the riverbank groves;

children.text: govindeti janārdaneti jagatāṃ nātheti kṛṣṇeti ca vyāhāraiḥ samayastadekamanasāṃ puṃsāmatikrāmati || 32 ||
children.translated_text: but for those single-minded ones, time passes with the utterances: '<s>Govinda</s>,' '<s>Janārdana</s>,' 'Lord of the worlds,' '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.' || 32 ||

children.text: ayācyamakreyamayātayāmamapācyamakṣayyamadurbharaṃ me /
children.translated_text: Not to be begged for, not to be purchased, not stale, not to be cooked, inexhaustible, not burdensome to me—

children.text: astyeva pātheyamitaḥ prayāṇe śrīkṛṣṇanāmamṛtabhāgadheyam || 33 ||
children.translated_text: Indeed, there is provision for the journey from here — the blessed portion of the nectar that is the name of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>.

children.text: yasya priyau śrutadharau kavilokagītau mittre dvijanmaparivāraśivāvabhūtām /
children.translated_text: He whose two beloved friends, learned in <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), celebrated in the world of poets, became <s>Śiva</s> in the retinue of the twice-born —

children.text: tenāmbujākṣacaraṇāmbujaṣaṭpadena rājñā kṛtā stutiriyaṃ kulaśekhareṇa || 34 ||
children.translated_text: by that king <s>Kulaśekhara</s>, a bee at the lotus feet of the lotus-eyed [Lord], this hymn of praise has been composed.

body.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Mukundamālā</s>, composed by the king <s>Śrī Kulaśekhara</s>.
